result.score_rationale: 48 -> 78. Of the four §4 economy blockers: (1) dies twice over (coins-per-kill generator AND the XP formula are both literal payload code), (3) Repair-Weapon cost dies outright, (4) token economy dies, (2) splits — sell-price formula dies, prosperity daily-sim survives but narrowed to "client renders, server computes". Three of six Ready-bullet "prices" turn out to be FORMULAS not constants; one Ready bullet is wrong in expectation (betting is EV-neutral, not a faucet); one is undercounted (five vendor generators, not two); one is uncited (IAP tiers, STILL_UNHELD). Two whole subsystems the ledger never mentions are fully held: the node×date-seeded trade-goods arbitrage loop, and the coin-purse cap ladder (1000..10000) that gives the whole economy its shape. Held back from 90+ by provenance: every AS3 cite is from the ANDROID bundle at clientVersion 0.682 (StatsManager.as:30) while the proven web target is v0.717; the web SWF is SWFDefender-protected and yields zero logic classes, so there is no same-version cross-check. result.score_rationale: 42 → 88. The ledger scored combat-core as "structure known, load-bearing numbers must be measured from footage or a dead build." That premise is void: `reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/` holds the complete, UNOBFUSCATED ActionScript 3 source of the combat system (925 default-package classes: MCSPlayer 4775 lines, NPCManager, InputManager, StatsManager, Damage, BattleUI, StageManager). Identity confirmed as Duels, not a sibling title (QueryManagerPIO.as:1872 `"name":"Straw Hat Samurai: Duels",`). ALL FIVE combat-core blockers are closed from source, not measurement: ① reach cap (full formula + units), ② crit multiplier (1.5 Light / 1.2 other, not 1.3 and not 3), ③ early-mob HP + starter weapon DMG + TTK (payload XML rows: hp 1, defense 0, weapon 1–2), ④ multi-target rule (full damage each, one hit per enemy per stroke), ⑤ Focus/crit gating (deterministic on a full reload bar, no proc). Beyond the blockers, one whole mechanic absent from the entire ledger was recovered (the ×1.2 stance triangle), two "Ready" bullets are wrong (crit 1.3; "shielder legs"), and two cross-lane blockers close as side effects (screen-shake catalogued, damage popups with exact colours). Not 100 because: (a) the readable source is the ANDROID/AIR payload — the web payload's logic is identifier-mangled (payload_export.log:9 `§1t398s0§`), so web-v0.717 parity is unproven, and one constant (`maxreload = 5*24` with a dead speed-scaled `baseReload`) smells like a mobile simplification; (b) per-slash animation start/active/recovery frames still live in the unopened `<animdata>` bindata sets (art-anim's ground); (c) `jumpThreshhold` and the provenance of the shipped `DASH_SLASH_PX=127` remain unverified — I did not find 127 anywhere in the slash path and will not call it wrong without evidence.

Four of the block's five blockers are answered outright by files already on disk, and every answer was re-verified in the obfuscated desktop v0.717 payload (reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/) before banking. Now held: the four element identities (FIRE/WIND/WATER/EARTH = stat ids 28/29/30/31, DEF 200-203) as class constants that do NOT need the missing string table; the complete 24-skill roster keyed to SkillManager constants; every elemental Chi cost and cooldown from skilldata.xml; the damage rule (elementATK x {0.8..1.2} by level, x1.5 on ultimates, ZERO physical component); per-element AoE radii 600/400/200/50 and launch types; the mitigation formula (flat subtraction with a hard min-1 floor); the element counter-wheel (your WATER atk IS your FIRE defence, etc.); the entire rebirth transaction down to the teleport target; Dan cap 9 with 9 title strings and 3 suffix tiers; and the complete Dragon Dance input (8-node click ring, two Heavens, the {1,2,4,6} gate, RNG-permuted statue sequences, 2 AP per attempt). claims.text: CROSS-LANE: the reach cap in stage pixels — combat-core's stated single most-needed value — is a function, found via how EnemyElite initialises its AI. baseSlashLength = 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5) * speed / (20 + speed)), i.e. 120 px at speed 0 rising asymptotically to 210 px, then multiplied per stance: Light 1.5x, Balanced 1.0->1.5x by mastery, Heavy 0.5->1.0x by mastery, floored at 100, and fed straight to InputManager.setMaxDistance — the drawn blade line's max length IS the reach. This also puts §3 correction #3 in doubt: 1.5:1.0:0.5 is exactly 3:2:1, so 300/200/100 reads as the mastery-ZERO values at baseSlashLength 200, not mastery-9 ceilings, and mastery raises Balanced/Heavy rather than being their cap.

result.score_rationale: Was 35. Four of the five §4 blockers are now fully closed from material already on disk (world bounds/geography, AP regen+cap, day length, gather/mine/farm yield+whiff+respawn), the fifth (sector↔room rule) is closed and independently confirmed by a video frame, and the whole overworld turns out to be a deterministic seeded-LCG generator rather than authored geography — verified closed-loop by regenerating the start territory's town name "Kasuta" and matching it to the frame that also reads TERRITORY (21,51). Three previously-unknown assets surfaced: the 63x72 Japan land mask (735 territories), a 676-line place-name table, and 69 authored trap rooms across 4 difficulty tiers. Held back from 90+ by three real gaps: src/config still contains zero world numbers (the Surface bullet survives), the string table is located but its binary is not extracted so every world NAME is still id-only, and the server-side prosperity daily-sim is genuinely gone. Also discounted slightly because the named AS3 is the Android port's payload, not the web build — mitigated but not eliminated by the three frame↔code agreements.

result.score_rationale: 56 -> 92. Five of the block's six blockers close outright. The headline: the ledger's #1 blocker "ALL AUDIO -- every SFX + music param is INFERRED, no composer sourced" and §6's "exact waveforms/envelopes are not [recoverable]" are both FALSE -- reference/preservation/shs3_android_payload.swf has been on disk since 2026-07-23 and decrypts with the game's own documented routine (key = filename.charCodeAt(1), ResourceManager.as:186,200) to yield 13 SFX + 13 music stems as MPEG-2.5 Layer III / 16 kbps / 11025 Hz mono MP3, named exactly as SoundManager/MusicManager call them. Font closes (Edo SZ, (c) 2008 Vic Fieger, embedded DefineFont3 with metrics). Blend modes close as a resolved NEGATIVE (6 blendMode hits corpus-wide, all Flex framework; game uses ColorTransform + BlurFilter + ColorMatrixFilter only). Screen-shake closes with the exact algorithm and call-site durations. Severed-limb deaths close (deathinhalf/deathnohand/deathnohead + seppuku_nohead). Beyond the blockers, the whole "Ready" list is under-claimed: it credits video MEASUREMENTS where the ORIGINAL source sits on disk -- 487 authored animations / 5,596 keyframes / 81,706 bone poses, ~2,400 vector shapes with literal fill hex, exact blood-particle and blade-FX params, per-layer depth-of-field blur, and a 24 fps engine clock that contests the "15fps pose latch". Residual -8 is two honest STILL_UNHELDs (per-hit hitstop; three unverifiable "Surface" bullets incl. scarf physics, which has zero counterpart in 2,768 decompiled classes) plus the fact that mapping the 19 rig node ids to shape symbols is real engineering. What remains here is engineering, not archaeology.

- **Ready:** currencies + guest start; all service prices; Forge/Reinforce/Rebirth/Writ costs; War-Room structure costs; crop 5–20c; IAP tiers; two-vendor tiers; gold has legit non-cash faucets (rebirth/tournament/betting).

The arbitrage subsystem the survey found goes from five nameless price curves to a shippable, named commodity ladder. '(Illegal)' on commodity 4 is a live lead: it is priced identically to Ceramics (200/30) yet flagged, so an offline port must decide whether legality was cosmetic flavour or a real risk/reward hook — a design question the ledger cannot even pose today.

new_findings.text: Cho-Han is EV-neutral only away from the purse ceiling: because the 2x payout goes through changeGold(), which clamps to getMaxCoins(), a win that would overflow the purse is silently truncated while the loss is always full — so at the cap the game is strictly EV-negative.

new_findings.lane_impact: economy. new_findings.text: itemdata.xml never writes <type>0</type>: the 153 armor-slot items carry no <type> element at all and rely on E4X coercing the missing node to 0, and there is a second band anomaly the survey missed.

Items with NO <type> element: 153, of which 152 sit in the 4xxx armor band and exactly 1 in 7xxx (id 7075). Missed anomaly: '<id>2211</id> <type>12</type> <name>4386</name> <unique>1</unique> <weight>0</weight> <nogive>1</nogive> <nodrop>1</nodrop>' — a 2xxx-band item typed 12.
new_findings.lane_impact: L3 — a port must default a missing <type> to 0 rather than reject the row, or it silently drops 152 armor items and one hat. Reproduce both authoring anomalies verbatim (7075 and 2211). Also note types 10 and 12 are not equipment-array indices despite the enum values, which is why Item.as:845 guards them.
